text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

The May white sugar contract in London recouped some of its losses at the close of business, the last session of its trading life, but still ended weaker on the day. May closed at $305.00 per tonne, down $1.50, after an afternoon of see-saw trading as players scrambled to bale out of the position before it went off the board. The second month August contract closed at $308.40 per tonne, down 50 cents. Overall volume amounted to a hefty 4,257 lots, bloated by against actuals and switch trades.

Light trade and commission house buying dragged May off its session low of $302.60 but the nearby May/August spread remained at a discount through most of the day while August/October and other spreads were at premiums. Raw sugar futures in New York closed lower amid steady speculative liquidation in the spot May contract and only sporadic buying by the trade, dealers said. May finished down 0.11 cent/lb at 11.13 cents/lb after trading from 11.21 to 11.10. Most-active July fell 0.12 cent/lb to 11.01 while the remaining months eased between 0.10 and 0.04 cent. The May/July spread closed at 0.12 compared with 0.11 on Monday.

USSIA - Russia will levy a 25 percent duty on all white sugar imports from May 15, but the tariff will not apply to Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, which have a customs treaty with Russia, a government decree said. The decree of April 11 said the 25 per cent tariff would be no lower than 0.07 Ecus per kg. Russia has been threatening since August 1996 to restrict refined sugar imports to 1.5 million tonnes a year, including a cap on Ukrainian origins of 1.15 million tonnes, to support struggling domestic refiners which run on beets and imported Cuban raws.

Imports of refined sugar from Ukraine have borne a 10 percent value-added tax since October 1, 1996. For countries outside the CIS the new trading rules will mean no change at all as the import tax on white sugar for them had been raised already to 25 percent in July 1995.

FRANCE - Sugar consumption in November 1996 amounted to 183,349 tonnes, raw value, up from 159,018 tonnes in November 1995. This brought cumulative consumption in the first two months of 1996/97 (October/November) up to 392,745 tonnes compared to 338,870 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total consumption in 1995/96 reached 2.217 million tonnes compared to 2.184 million in 1994/95.

CYPRUS - Sugar imports in calendar 1996 reached 33,633 tonnes, slightly down on the previous year's 34,191 tonnes but up on the 1994 result of 32,600 tonnes. The major countries of origin in calendar year 1996 were the UK with 14,754 tonnes whites against 15,591 and Germany with 12,469 tonnes, down from 13,647 tonnes.

TURKEY - State-run sugar holding Turkseker has so far exported 60,000 tonnes of white sugar from its 1996/97 (September/August) production and will sell another 40,000 tonnes, Industry Minister Yalim Erez said. He reiterated the view that Turkey will not need any sugar imports this year or in 1997/98. Turkseker officials said earlier the company was planning to sell some 200,000 tonnes in calendar year 1997 from 1996 output as well as using its stock of an estimated one million tonnes.

EUROPE - The beet belt in western Europe where drillings were mostly completed this week again saw below average precipitation in the week ended April 15. The dry weather is expected to continue at least for another week. Crops are in no immediate danger from the persistent lack of rain, but more moisture will need to return in May to ensure stable germination and early development. Moisture reserves in the eastern belt are adequate due to periodic showers in the past month.

State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp said it will tender on April 22 in New York city for a 30,000-tonne shipment of raw sugar. The shipment is slated for June 5 to June 20 arrival. The official said the tender will be invitation-only.
